name: Security & Permission
checks: All protected routes have authentication (middleware / route guard)
All non-public routes must be intercepted — no route is accidentally exposed without auth middleware
Sensitive data read/write has authorization (RLS / DAL / policy engine)
No client-trusted identity parameters without server-side verification (`userId`, `orgId`, `shopId`)
All webhooks have signature verification
Payment/webhook flows have idempotency (using provider event ID or equivalent)
API responses do not leak internal info (stack traces, internal paths, secret fragments)
Error handlers fail closed (deny on exception), NOT fail open (continue on exception)
Lockfile exists, committed, pinning exact dependency versions
Hash verification of dependencies — dependency integrity verified via hash/checksum, not just version pinning
No long-lived credentials where short-lived identity is possible
External writes have audit trail (`user_id` + `timestamp` + `trace_id`)
Automation systems have emergency stop / kill switch mechanism
Signed commits — code provenance is verifiable through commit signing
Dual control for high-risk operations — privileged operations (key rotation, production data deletion, permission escalation) require two-party approval
Immutable logs (WORM) for critical operations — audit logs for financial, auth, and data-deletion events cannot be retroactively modified
Network security: default deny ingress, egress filtering, critical zone isolation — network posture follows least-privilege principle
CI pipeline dependency audit: automated vulnerability scan on dependencies in CI [Growth
Production DB dashboard write restriction: production DB writes restricted to application service accounts only, not human dashboards [Growth
Rate limiting on sensitive endpoints: auth, payment, and admin endpoints have rate limits [Growth
SBOM auto-generation in CI: Software Bill of Materials generated automatically during build [Scale
Incident Response Playbook formalized: documented response procedures for security incidents [Scale
Public Bucket Audit scheduled: periodic audit ensuring no storage buckets are unintentionally public [Scale
Infrastructure scanning integrated: automated infra scanning (IaC, container images) in pipeline [Scale
Dependency updates staged rollouts: dependency updates deployed progressively, not all-at-once [Scale

checks.check: Auth is applied through unified wrappers rather than re-implemented per route.
Each service has its own identity with fine-grained permissions rather than sharing a broad credential.

anti_patterns: Catch-all error handlers that fail open instead of fail closed
Client-trusted identity parameters without server-side verification
Long-lived credentials where short-lived identity exchange is available
No kill switch for privileged automation
Privileged writes with no audit trail
Secret material present in repo or unvalidated runtime paths
